name: move
purpose: Copies, clears, or evaluates a value into a destination.

variants.behavior: Copies or clears the selected destination and continues. A node moved into a temporary variable can remain a reference to that node. Dynamic evaluation uses the current expression and XML context.
constraints: Use a literal, relative expression, null, or a quoted temporary-variable expression as the source. A destination can be a temporary variable, data-area path, or evaluate(...) path.
A bare $name move source converts to a data-area source named name. A double-$ source fails conversion; a double-$ destination becomes a data-area destination.
The escape(...) instruction is not preserved by the BPA conversion. Literal source text may contain host %NAME substitutions.
Move destinations use the data-area path language. The root cannot start with / or +; append segments belong below a named root.

A plain single-quoted destination is recognized by the shared syntax but is not a usable data-area path. Write a destination path in double quotes; single quotes retain literal delimiters rather than selecting that path.
errors: A double-$ move source cannot be converted to a browser instruction.
A destination must have a named data-area root; leading / or + is outside the destination-path language.

variants.behavior: Uses the browser move operation with legacy null and empty-selection rules. A legacy clear is represented as a data-area-to-data-area move from %NULL. A source encoded with the modern null source kind does not automatically obtain that legacy clear behavior.
constraints: Use the legacy structured null representation when clearing data. Do not assume textual move null has the same result as ordinary browser engine 1.
A direct path-selection result with no nodes can be an empty string rather than null; complex-expression fallback behavior depends on the browser path used.
Quoted "$name" reads a local value. Bare $name remains a data-area source, $$source cannot be converted, and $$destination becomes a data-area destination.
The escape(...) marker is not retained by browser conversion. Destination paths use the browser data-area rules.

A plain single-quoted destination is recognized by the shared syntax but is not a usable data-area path. Write a destination path in double quotes; single quotes retain literal delimiters rather than selecting that path.
errors: An unsupported global source or destination shape fails.

variants.behavior: Evaluates the source and writes a local variable, request-context variable, or schema-aware data-area destination. A selected element assigned to a local variable remains the evaluated element; later changes may be visible through that reference. Normal execution continues with the next statement.
constraints: Use quoted "$name" to read a local variable. A bare $name source is treated as the XPath text name; evaluate($name) and escape($name) explicitly read the local variable before applying their operation.
$$name reads or writes a request-context string value. A list cannot be assigned to a request-context variable; an element contributes its text content.

evaluate(...) first resolves an expression or path string and then evaluates it. escape(...) HTML-escapes a resolved path or local-variable value. Wrapping a $$ source does not apply these transformations: its global read is handled first.
A null data-area move clears according to the destination schema. A null source assigned to a local variable supplies the text null; it is not a universal variable-deletion operation.
Destination paths have a named data-area root. Data-area target navigation uses the host destination-path rules and XPath 1 selection even when the source expression uses XPath 2.

A plain single-quoted destination is recognized by the shared syntax but is not a usable data-area path. Write a destination path in double quotes; single quotes retain literal delimiters rather than selecting that path.
errors: An unresolved dynamic source fails. Unsupported target shapes fail. A null source is not permitted for a move-by-name target ending in /*.

variants.behavior: Evaluates and assigns using the server move rules. When a selected element is assigned directly to a local variable, the element is copied into a fresh document. That variable therefore does not retain the source element identity. The copy rule concerns an element value and does not promise deep copying of every possible result shape.
constraints: Use quoted "$name" for a local-variable read; bare $name is evaluated as the XPath text name. evaluate($name) and escape($name) explicitly resolve the local variable.
$$name accesses request-context string values. A list cannot be stored there; an element contributes its text content.
evaluate(...) resolves and evaluates a dynamic expression. escape(...) HTML-escapes a resolved value. A global-source read occurs before either wrapper transformation.
Source expressions use XPath 2. Destination navigation retains the host destination-path rules and XPath 1 selection.
A null data-area move clears according to schema rules; a null source assigned to a local variable supplies the text null. It does not delete the variable.

A plain single-quoted destination is recognized by the shared syntax but is not a usable data-area path. Write a destination path in double quotes; single quotes retain literal delimiters rather than selecting that path.
errors: An unresolved dynamic source, unsupported destination, list-to-global assignment, or null move-by-name target fails.

name: if
purpose: Chooses one statement block according to a condition.

variants.behavior: Chooses the true body only when the browser condition result equals true; otherwise takes the alternate path. Execution rejoins after the selected body.
constraints: The condition is a quoted expression inside parentheses. Close the construct with end-if and a semicolon.

variants.behavior: Evaluates the condition, executes the selected block, and then continues unless that block transfers control or terminates. A missing else means no alternate body.
constraints: The single result must be true or false, case-insensitively. A blank or absent result is false. Use an explicit Boolean comparison for numeric, textual, or node values.
Expressions use XPath 1 in server-1 and XPath 2 in server-2 and server-3.
errors: A nonblank result other than true or false is an error, rather than an implicit truthy value.

name: for
purpose: Visits selected values in a statement block.

variants.behavior: Visits selected nodes, exposing each node through the loop variable. The body begins after the expanded loop instruction. Completing a loop that has iterated clears its variable; this does not establish that an empty selection clears a prior value. A result needed afterward belongs in a separate variable.
constraints: An empty selection executes the body zero times. The loop variable is available in the body and is cleared after an iterated loop finishes.
Quotes inside selection predicates can be removed during conversion, changing their meaning. Dynamic or variable-based selection requires the intended XML context. A jump out retains iteration state.

variants.behavior: Iterates each member of a collection, or once for a scalar result. Each iteration assigns the loop variable and executes the body. A null or empty result executes no iterations. Normal completion leaves the last assigned loop value in local storage; an empty loop does not assign a new value.
constraints: Selection uses the current engine expression rules. Use the direct quoted selection expression; the evaluate(...) marker does not add a second server evaluation of the selected result.
Predicate quotes are retained on the server execution path. A jump out propagates the requested transfer instead of finishing the remaining iterations.
A loop variable should have a distinct name from values that must survive unchanged.

name: goto

errors: An unknown or out-of-scope destination fails.

variants.behavior: Plain terminate completes the current server script normally. constraints: A service-script caller can continue after normal return. An error propagates through server invocation unless a surrounding host boundary handles it.

errors: An invalid message, substitution, or error-element reference can fail. A caller without map-completion support cannot fulfill terminate with map.

variants.behavior: Invokes a public zero-argument method on the current script's compiled Groovy instance. The host supplies the current data-area root, invocation context, and schema metadata before calling it. A method return value is not assigned by this command; use the shared script context to exchange values.
constraints: The script must supply Groovy members and the host must permit Groovy compilation and execution.

Use a literal method name, such as invokeGroovy 'prepareResult'. Although variable and expression operands are recognized by the shared syntax, this invocation uses their stored name text rather than evaluating them dynamically.
A successful call resumes at the next Edit Data statement. This mixed-script integration does not select the pure Groovy engine.

In supporting host releases, Groovy members may construct restricted expression arguments with concatenateGroovyStrings. Confirm the helper and its argument tracking on the target host; the script engine or Groovy language version alone does not establish availability. The helper result, a local variable declared or assigned from it, or an alias of that variable can supply such an argument; the helper arguments remain subject to host restrictions. This host API is not an Edit Data command.
errors: A missing compiled instance, missing public zero-argument method, or method exception fails the call.

variants.behavior: This is an Edit Data command, not a statement in the Groovy language. A script using the Groovy engine uses its Groovy entry point and host APIs.
constraints: Use the Groovy integration profile for lifecycle and host-access rules.
